findings.text: 在 ACP 编辑器中直接使用 DSH 的 Agent 和工具，减少向独立客户端搬运任务。见 [Q01](#research-q01)。
ACP 请求创建/恢复 DSH Agent，followup/steer 驱动原循环，日志投影为文字、工具结果、计划和终止事件。见 [Q01](#research-q01)。
定向核查启动、原生服务、会话提交、事件投影、审批取消、MCP 生命周期与多根文件/沙箱接线。未全审认证 UI、所有协议扩展、历史日志迁移、全部附件类型和跨平台兼容；未安装或运行目标。
package 0.4.40，Apache-2.0；包含 dsh-acp 独立 bin 和原生插件/stdio 模块。未核对发布制品。

| 依赖 | 作用 | 必要性 | 条件与边界 |
|---|---|---|---|
| ACP 编辑器 | 协议 UI | 必需 | 客户端能力决定可呈现事件 |
| DSH 运行时 | Agent、模型、工具 | 必需 | 原生宿主或独立打包运行时 |
| Node / 凭据 | 启动及模型访问 | 必需 | Node >=22.15；未执行认证 |
| MCP 服务 | 扩展工具 | 可选 | 进程共享、同名可替换 |

| 阶段 | 现金 | 人工 | 未知及控制 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 首次 | 未测 | 编辑器、运行时、凭据配置 | 一次性工作区核验 |
| 持续 | 模型及外部工具费用未测 | 版本维护和审核 | 不推算节省 |
| 失败恢复 | 重试调用未测 | 核查日志与真实副作用 | 不盲目重发 |
| 退出 | 无独立测算 | 停进程、保留或清理日志配置 | 会话关闭不清 MCP |
在一次性工作区逐次审批，先读后做可恢复修改，核对实际宿主、目录及 MCP；异常停进程检查副作用。见 [Q04](#research-q04)。

| 结果 | 源码支持 | 尚未确认 |
|---|---|---|
| 编辑器驱动 | 真实 Agent followup/steer | 具体编辑器完整体验 |
| 工具可追踪 | 调用、结果和终止投影 | 执行成功及语义正确 |
| 多根操作 | 文件与沙箱范围接线 | 各平台实际约束 |
| 效率 | 减少搬运的机制 | 时间、正确率、全部成本 |
传输无关服务、原生/独立入口及目录真实约束可借鉴；共享 MCP 和会话审批策略必须向使用者讲清。见 [Q02](#research-q02)。
实际增量是 DSH 会话及事件语义到 ACP 的双入口适配，含多根写范围与审批桥接；自主循环和模型能力继承宿主。见 [Q01](#research-q01)、[Q03](#research-q03)。
会话始终允许会关闭该会话后续审批，MCP 挂载却按进程共享并可同名替换；多会话不能直接当隔离域，取消不撤销副作用。见 [Q02](#research-q02)。
给每会话提供有效宿主、模型、写根、审批和 MCP 指纹回执，验证能否减少环境误判；现有 UI 若已同等明确则推翻。见 [Q04](#research-q04)。

technical.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)协议适配属于常规组合，novelty25%；事件、会话和多根权限接线构成局部完整机制，mechanism50%。仍强依赖 DSH 服务及 ACP，transferability50%；减少任务搬运但需要双端兼容，simplification50%，无比较实验支持75%。

business.rationale: [Q03](#research-q03)把既有开发任务接入编辑器，workflow25%，结果仍是代码任务交付，delivery0。协议接入降低受客户端限制用户的入口障碍，reach25%，无新群体采用证据支持50%。没有完整费用与合格任务对照，economics=null。

recommendation.reason: 已有 DSH 使用需求的单人开发者可在一次性工作区核验 ACP 编辑器接入。相比复制任务到独立客户端，它复用真实 Agent 并返回工具结果，但须逐次审批并固定受信 MCP 配置。若目录、权限或挂载与预期不符，应停进程核查实际修改，再回到原 DSH 客户端。

scenario.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)有具体编辑器任务与复制替代办法，达50%；缺少真实频率与阻塞程度，不达75%。

advantage.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)跟到 followup、工具结果与终止，较纯文本搬运有50%增量；[Q02](#research-q02)共享挂载和权限范围限制，未测结果改善，不达75%。

evidence.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)至[Q03](#research-q03)追踪双入口、Agent、权限、取消及多根实际接线，达到源码50%上限；未运行客户端，不达75%。

cost.rationale: [Q03](#research-q03)可识别运行时/调用/恢复负担并用一次性目录退回原客户端，超过25%；版本及外部工具组合仍需维护，未支持75%轻负担。

deepseek-harness-acp

Use DeepSeek Harness from Agent Client Protocol clients such as Zed and Backchat.

--- The adapter composes the harness **in-process** and maps its session-event log onto the full ACP vocabulary: streamed text and reasoning, tool calls with diffs and display terminals, plans, permission requests, session modes, config options, slash commands, skills, and MCP servers. Credentials never touch your editor config — it reuses the key you saved in the dsh Web UI, or `dsh-acp login` saves one to the same store. ## One package, standalone or plugin | | **A · dsh profile plugin (recommended)** | **B · Standalone server** | |---|---|---| | Best for | Normal installation and upgrades | Connecting an ACP client without managing a dsh profile | | Install | `dsh plugin --profile acp add @openma/deepseek-harness-acp@latest` | `npm i -g @openma/deepseek-harness-acp` | | Zed runs | `dsh --profile acp` | `dsh-acp` | | Harness | The dsh that owns the profile | Your installed dsh, then the package's locked private runtime | | Composition | dsh-base + this bundle + your profile's own patches | dsh-base + this bundle (profile machinery booted in-process) | Both shapes share `$DSH_HOME`: the same credential store, settings, presets, and session logs as `dsh web` — conversations started in the Web UI can be listed and loaded from the editor. Other dsh surfaces can mount the transport-independent `@openma/deepseek-harness-acp/plugin` on their Base Host tree and own the transport adapter. The TUI profile uses this path: it starts a separate TUI Client process and connects ACP over that process's standard stdin/stdout; it does not start `dsh-acp` or use an in-process Client stream. The package is therefore not only a CLI wrapper. It is also the ACP surface plugin used by other dsh applications: one Host composition can expose the same sessions, tools, presets, skills, and persistence through a transport chosen by the surface. ### DSH compatibility This release supports **`@deepseek-ai/dsh` `>=0.1.7-rc.2`** — a minimum-version floor declared in `engines.dsh` (the field dsh's own plugin loader checks, with prereleases included), never an exact-version list. It is deliberately not a `@deepseek-ai/dsh` peer dependency: npm and pnpm match peer ranges without prereleases, so a peer floor would reject every dsh prerelease. A newer dsh is always attempted: API differences between dsh generations are feature-detected where they are used (for example dsh 0.2.1's `subagents.drainDescendants` versus 0.2.0's `drainContinuableDescendants`), and a dsh newer than the newest tested version (`0.2.1-rc.2`) only logs a warning. Only a dsh below the floor is refused. CI exercises the tested profile matrix (`runtime/compatibility.json`) plus the `next` dist-tag. A competing load/resume returns a standard JSON-RPC error. Closing the session or exiting the owner process allows another process to resume it. Every process writing shared sessions must use a fixed backend; older hosts do not participate in this lock. Restoring historical sessions uses the host's V3 migration, which preserves the original log. Upgraded sessions cannot be read by older hosts. Add dsh plugins to that profile to change the agent composition instead of forking the ACP server: providers and models join the live catalog, commands and skills join the advertised session surface, tools and subagents appear through standard `session/update`, and the same session persistence remains available to every surface. For applications embedding ACP, the public package entries are: | Export | Role | |---|---| | `@openma/deepseek-harness-acp/plugin` | Complete Host-side surface plugin. This is the shape used by [`@openma/deepseek-harness-tui`](https://github.com/openma-ai/deepseek-harness-tui): ACP stays on the Base Host tree while a separate TUI Client process owns its own Cordis tree. Adding a Cordis service does not automatically invent a wire method. Advertise support in `initialize` metadata, with a namespaced and versioned capability such as `_meta.dsh.cordis.protocol`. 2. Carry annotations on standard messages in namespaced `_meta` fields when no new request is needed. 3. Name custom JSON-RPC requests and notifications with a leading underscore, and send them only after both peers negotiated the matching capability. 4. Keep the standard ACP path complete. A client that does not advertise an extension must still get normal sessions, prompts, updates, cancellation, auth, and config options. #### DSH tool result values The [ACP metadata registry][metadata-registry] is the authoritative list of every `_meta` field this adapter reads or emits. It records direction, carrier, shape, negotiation requirements, and replay behavior, including native DSH tool values at `_meta.dsh.toolResult.value`. [metadata-registry]: https://github.com/openma-ai/deepseek-harness-acp/blob/main/docs/metadata.md The current package applies this pattern to the built-in `_dsh/cordis/*` family used by the TUI for Client capability discovery, dynamic Package lifecycle, and package-private Host/Client RPC. It is an explicit, versioned extension—not a synchronization of Cordis plugin ids, fibers, or `inject` across processes. The bridge's internal method registry is not currently a public arbitrary-extension API; new extension families should first define a stable capability, ownership, lifecycle, and fallback contract. ## Authentication No keys in editor config, no secrets pasted into chat. ACP clients follow the protocol: `initialize` advertises the **Agent Auth** methods the client declared it can use. 1. **API key** — `api-key`, or `api-key:` per live route. The client may pass `_meta["api-key"].apiKey`. 2. **Terminal** — `terminal-login`, when the client declares `clientCapabilities.auth.terminal` (or `_meta["terminal-auth"]`). The client runs the advertised `dsh-acp login` command itself — the adapter never supplies a command path — and the saved key is picked up on the next `authenticate` or `session/new`. 3. **Browser** — `browser`, only when the client declares `clientCapabilities.elicitation.url`. The adapter starts a localhost sign-in page and hands its URL to the client through url elicitation — headless, SSH, and WSL sessions all see the URL. The secret never travels over ACP; the page's own timeout bounds the wait, and a decline or cancel ends the flow with `auth_required` instead of hanging. 4. **Custom gateway** — `gateway`, only when the client opts in with `clientCapabilities.auth._meta.gateway === true`. The client sends `_meta.gateway` `{ baseUrl, headers, providerName? }`. The adapter writes credentials to the harness store. Missing credentials fail `session/new` and `session/prompt` with `auth_required` (`-32000`) carrying `data.authMethods` — the same advertised list — so the client can open its auth UI from any failure. Typing a native auth command (`/login`, `/logout`) gets a plain "isn't available in this environment" reply pointing at the client's sign-in/sign-out and ends the turn — it is never advertised, never reaches the model, never changes credentials, and never returns `auth_required`. `logout` is scoped to one provider route — the one named by `_meta.provider`, or the active provider when omitted — and clears only that provider's stored key and gateway base-URL. Re-authenticating overwrites the same provider's credential; authenticating a second provider adds alongside the first; `dsh-acp login --provider ` replaces it out of band. The active method, provider, and credential name are pushed to the client as `_auth/status_update` whenever they change. 1. **Harness credential store** — `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml` (mode 600), the file the dsh Web UI writes; hot-reloaded. Save a key with `dsh-acp login [--provider ]`, or the Web UI (Settings → Models). 2. **Process environment** — `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` / `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL` (and the matching `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` for those routes) in the environment that launches the agent. The credential gate is the **current provider route**. An Anthropic-only store is enough for an Anthropic session; a DeepSeek key does not unlock another provider. ## Features - **Streaming** — assistant text and reasoning deltas; assembled-message fallback. - **Images** — `promptCapabilities.image` is advertised when the composition mounts `ctx.attachments` (dsh-base does). ACP `image` blocks are validated, stored with `saveImage`, and kept in wire order with surrounding text. `resource_link` stays a textual file pointer. - **Tool calls** — ACP kinds, human titles, file locations, real diffs from fs-tool hunks, raw input/output; command output on a **display terminal** when the client supports one, fenced output otherwise. - **Permission presets as session modes** — `read-only` / `workspace-write` / `danger-full-access`, each a named `{sandbox, approval}` pair recorded as a durable session fact (also exposed as a config option for clients that only render those). - **Agent composition** — when the profile mounts `agentPresets`, an uncategorized config option `id: "agent"` lists the roster (`standard` / `code` / `minimal` / `cordis`, plus user copies). Switching rebuilds the agent live with history preserved. Authoring (copy/rm) stays on the Web settings page; there is no `/preset` slash. - **Live model catalog** — providers × models from the running composition (third-party providers added in the Web UI appear immediately), plus reasoning-effort selection that follows your product default. Model option ids are stable: bare model ids while one provider is registered, `provider::model` as soon as there are several — never keyed on the *current default* provider (which every switch rewrites), so an id a client cached keeps working. Bare ids are still accepted on input and resolve to the provider that serves them. - **Slash commands** — adapter built-ins (`/status`, `/model`) plus the harness command registry (`/compact`, `/goal`, `/permission`, `/plan`, …) executed without a model turn, plus **skills** (`/skill-name` — the harness's own invocation gesture). Login and logout are ACP methods, not chat commands. - **Plans & usage** — `todo_write` snapshots as ACP plans; token accounting as `usage_update` and per-turn usage. - **Sessions** — `session/resume` restores a durable session without replaying its transcript; `session/load` remains the full-history path. Also supports `session/list`, silent restore when a client prompts an old session after an agent restart, and titles as `session_info_update`. **Multi-root sessions** are supported through the bundled multi-root plugin: `initialize` advertises `sessionCapabilities.additionalDirectories: {}`, and `session/new`, `session/load`, `session/resume`, and `session/fork` accept absolute directory paths (`cwd` stays the base for relative paths). Additional roots are readable in every mode and writable under `workspace-write` (not under `read-only`); omitted or empty input on `session/new` is exactly the single-root path. The list is persisted as a session plugin record: `load`/`resume`/`fork` restore it when the client omits `additionalDirectories`, while a non-empty request replaces it. The plugin replaces the core `fs-sandbox`/`sandbox` rows with thin in-tree subclasses and widens bwrap/Landlock/Seatbelt profiles; a profile shape it cannot widen fails closed rather than silently dropping the roots. Residual limits: the Windows ACL backend cannot widen its singular workspace grant (additional-root writes are unsupported there, though reads still work), Windows UNC/device paths are refused, and widening is coupled to the profile shapes emitted by `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-local`. - **Fork** — `initialize` advertises `sessionCapabilities.fork: {}` and `agentCapabilities._meta.jetbrains.air.fork = { version: 1, inclusive: true }` (deep-merged next to `dsh.cordis`). `session/fork` creates a new session id and leaves the source session unchanged. Without `_meta.jetbrains.air.fork`, the new session copies the source's committed log. With that block, the copy keeps the selected assistant message and everything before it, and drops every later message. `messageId` is the ACP id `:` (a `:segment:` id is also matched as ``). An optional `messageFingerprint` (`sha256:` + SHA-256 of the assistant text) and 1-based `messageOccurrence` disambiguate. A bad version, a bad fingerprint, a missing id, or a point that is not in the log is JSON-RPC `-32602` — the adapter does not silently copy the whole session. Unknown session ids and subagent child sessions are also `-32602`. Only persisted assistant messages are fork points; a running turn's live stream is ignored. If the selected message itself contains tool calls, those calls are removed from the copied message (their results are stored after the message, so keeping the calls would leave an illegal transcript and would make `session/load` replay continue past the message). Tool calls and results from earlier messages stay. `session/load` on the new session replays through that assistant message and no further; `session/prompt` continues from there. The fork response carries the same `modes` and `configOptions` shape as `session/new`. - **MCP servers** — per-session `mcpServers` mount `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` instances (stdio + streamable HTTP); tools join as `mcp____`; a failing server never takes the session down. - **Steering** — the initialize response advertises `_meta.steering.supported: true`. If that turn ends before injection, the response is `{ outcome: "promptRequired", reason: "noRunningTurn" }` and the client sends an ordinary `session/prompt`. Omitting `idleBehavior` uses the same behavior. Concurrent `session/prompt` steering remains supported. - **Real cancellation** — `session/cancel` interrupts the live turn through the harness agent. ## Configuration Flags win over environment variables, which win over defaults.
